subject: Re: Order Form — pricing schedule, activation escrow & tax residency
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@cloudgrid.com>

Cc: CloudGrid Procurement <billing@cloudgrid.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — invoicing cadence and tax withholding

Hi David,

Thanks for sending over the updated order form. A couple of items came up during procurement review that we need to confirm before we can issue a PO:

1) Invoicing cadence: CloudGrid needs invoices split into two line items — (a) activation / onboarding fee, and (b) monthly usage commitments. Our accounting wants the activation fee invoiced at contract execution but held in escrow until go-live is confirmed.

2) Minimum commit: We see the tiered minimum commit ladder. Can Redwood support invoicing the first tranche at signing and the remainder on a quarterly basis tied to consumption?

3) Taxes/withholding: Because CloudGrid is registered in multiple EU subsidiaries, procurement requested a clause that allows for withholding tax where applicable and a list of required tax certificates for crediting.

We attached CloudGrid's standard PO template and a quick markup of section 4 (pricing schedule). Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Patel
Director, Procurement
CloudGrid Inc.

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. We can accommodate most of these but need to align internally on a couple of points and propose precise language for the order form and MSA redline:

- Activation fee escrow: We can invoice at signing and place funds into an escrow account for release upon mutually agreed go-live acceptance. I'll attach draft escrow language and ask legal to confirm.

- Tranche invoicing for minimum commit: We can structure first tranche at signing, then quarterly invoices for remaining tranches. Laura, can finance confirm whether quarterly invoicing will require a different billing entity or PO fields?

- Withholding/tax certificates: Karthik, can legal draft a short clause permitting tax withholding where mandated by law and enumerate required evidence (tax residency certificates, W-8/W-9 equivalents, or EU VAT registration numbers)? Also flag any risk with escrow release tied to tax documentation.

Next steps: I will send an internal redline and the proposed language by EOD tomorrow and share a DocuSign link once CloudGrid confirms. If you prefer a call, we can do 30 minutes on Thursday.

Thanks,
David
David Kim

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Order form questions — invoicing cadence and tax withholding

Folks — drafting notes below for proposed order form/MSA language. Draft will be attached as a separate redline.

1) Escrow for activation fee
Proposed: "Customer shall pay the activation fee at execution. Redwood will hold such fee in an escrow account administered by [Escrow Agent]. Funds will be released to Redwood upon demonstration of Go-Live as defined in Schedule A or within 90 days if Customer does not provide reasonable evidence of readiness, subject to dispute resolution."

Reason: preserves Redwood's cash flow while addressing CloudGrid's request. Need to confirm escrow agent and fee for escrow administration. Finance to confirm impact.

2) Tranche invoicing for minimum commit
Proposed: "The Minimum Commitment shall be invoiced in tranches as set forth in the pricing schedule: initial tranche due at signing; subsequent tranches invoiced quarterly in arrears. Each invoice will indicate the tranche number and corresponding contract period."

Note: This requires mapping tranche dates to calendar quarters in the order form; Laura, please add typical invoice memo fields the accounting team needs (entity, remit-to, tax ID).

3) Taxes/withholding and certificates
Proposed: "If applicable under local law, Customer may withhold taxes on payments due to Redwood. Customer shall provide Redwood with valid tax residency documentation or other certificates necessary for Redwood to claim treaty benefits or tax credits within 30 days of request. Failure to provide required documentation may result in delayed release of escrow funds for activation fees until resolved."

Risk: tying escrow release to receipt of tax certificates could create operational delay. Suggest limiting delays to a short cure window (30 days) and allowing Redwood to escalate to dispute resolution if outstanding.

I'll attach a redline of the Order Form (pricing sheet and clauses) for internal review.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts

Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence and tax withholding

Sarah — attaching our proposed redline to the Order Form and a short SOW indicating milestone definitions (attached: CloudGrid_OrderForm_redlines_20270916.docx; redlines_orderform_20270916.xlsx; CloudGrid_SOW_v3.pdf). Key changes summarized below: 

- Activation fee: invoiced at signing, funds placed into escrow (details in §2.1 of redline).
- Minimum commit: initial tranche at signing; subsequent tranches invoiced quarterly in arrears (pricing sheet tab "Tranches").
- Taxes/withholding: Customer may withhold where law requires; Customer must provide tax residency documentation within 30 days of request. Escrow release tied to go-live acceptance; if tax documentation is missing, release may be delayed but Redwood may pursue dispute resolution after a 30-day cure window.

Action items for CloudGrid: please review attached redline and indicate whether you can accept the escrow agent model or propose an alternative (evidence of bank-managed escrow is fine). Also confirm whether CloudGrid can provide tax residency certificates within 30 days post-signing.

DocuSign: once redlines are agreed, we'll upload the final order form and send the DocuSign link.

Best,
David

David,

Thanks — the proposed language is close. A few clarifications from our side before we finalize: 

- Escrow agent: CloudGrid prefers using our bank-managed escrow account (bank details provided in the PO) rather than third-party escrow. Is Redwood able to accept bank-held escrow?
- Tax certificates: We can provide most EU VAT registrations and tax residency forms but will need 45 days for one subsidiary (AT subsidiary requires additional signature routing). Can you accept 45 days for that entity only?
- Net terms: CloudGrid procurement prefers Net 45 for new vendor onboarding. Will Redwood accept Net 45 for the invoiced tranches?

If you can confirm these three items we can route a PO. We can also do a short call Monday to finalize details.

Regards,
Sarah
